ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus $ABCD$ is 2, and $\angle ADC=120^\circ$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of side $AB$, and point $P$ is a moving point on the diagonal $AC$. What is the minimum value of $PB+PE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect BD, DE, and DE intersects AC at point P$^{\prime}$. Connect BP$^{\prime}$,

$\because$ rhombus ABCD,

$\therefore$ point B and point D are symmetrical about AC,

$\therefore$ DP$^{\prime}$=BP$^{\prime}$,

$\therefore$ P$^{\prime}$B + P$^{\prime}$E = DP$^{\prime}$ + P$^{\prime}$E = DE,

$\because$ the line segment between two points is the shortest,

$\therefore$ the minimum value of P$^{\prime}$B + P$^{\prime}$E is equal to the length of DE;

$\because$ rhombus ABCD,

$\therefore$ DC$\parallel$AB, AD=AB,

$\therefore$ $\angle$ADC + $\angle$DAB = 180$^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle$DAB = 60$^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\triangle$ADB is an equilateral triangle,

$\because$ point E is the midpoint of AB,

$\therefore$ DE $\perp$ AB, BE=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=1, BD=AB=2,

In $\triangle$BDE, $BE=\sqrt{BD^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}}=\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore$ the minimum value of PB+PE is $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: Use the reflection shortest-path route. First read the diagram as a rhombus ordered A-D-C-B, with diagonal AC drawn, P constrained to lie on AC, and E on side AB. From the text, use side length 2, angle ADC = 120 degrees, and E is the midpoint of AB. In a rhombus, diagonal AC is the perpendicular bisector/symmetry axis for vertices B and D, so for any P on AC, PB = PD. Thus PB + PE = PD + PE. The shortest broken path from D to P to E with P on AC occurs when D, P, E are collinear, so the minimum equals DE, where P is the intersection of DE with AC. To compute DE, use DC parallel AB to get angle DAB = 60 degrees; since AD = AB = 2, triangle ADB is equilateral, so BD = 2. Since E is the midpoint of AB, BE = 1 and DE is the altitude/median in the equilateral triangle, hence DE = sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3).

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and one-variable minimization. From the diagram, orient the rhombus so AB is a horizontal side and AD makes a 60-degree angle with AB, consistent with angle ADC = 120 degrees. From the text, set A = (0,0), B = (2,0), D = (1,sqrt(3)), C = (3,sqrt(3)), and E = (1,0). A general point P on diagonal AC can be written as P(t) = (3t, sqrt(3)t), 0 <= t <= 1. Then PB + PE = sqrt((3t-2)^2 + 3t^2) + sqrt((3t-1)^2 + 3t^2). Minimize this convex function of t. Differentiate: f'(t) = (12t-6)/PB + (12t-3)/PE. At t = 1/3, P = (1, sqrt(3)/3), giving PB = 2/sqrt(3), PE = 1/sqrt(3), and f'(1/3)=0. Since the sum of distances from a point moving on a segment to fixed points is convex, this critical point is the minimum. Therefore the minimum is 2/sqrt(3) + 1/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3).
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure shows rhombus ABCD with A on the left, C on the right, D above, and B below. The diagonal AC is drawn, and point P lies on AC. Point E lies on side AB, visually at its midpoint, and the segments PE and PB are drawn.

Reasoning: Following the coordinate method, place A = (0,0), B = (2,0). Since the rhombus has side length 2 and angle ADC = 120°, the adjacent angle DAB is 60°, so set D = (1, sqrt(3)) and C = (3, sqrt(3)). Since E is the midpoint of AB, E = (1,0).

A point P on diagonal AC can be parametrized by P(t) = (3t, sqrt(3)t), where 0 <= t <= 1. Then
PB = sqrt((3t - 2)^2 + 3t^2),
PE = sqrt((3t - 1)^2 + 3t^2).
So define
f(t) = PB + PE = sqrt((3t - 2)^2 + 3t^2) + sqrt((3t - 1)^2 + 3t^2).

Differentiate:
f'(t) = (12t - 6)/PB + (12t - 3)/PE.
At t = 1/3, P = (1, sqrt(3)/3). Then
PB = sqrt((-1)^2 + 1/3) = 2/sqrt(3),
PE = sqrt(0^2 + 1/3) = 1/sqrt(3).
Thus
f'(1/3) = (-2)/(2/sqrt(3)) + 1/(1/sqrt(3)) = -sqrt(3) + sqrt(3) = 0.

Because the sum of distances from a point moving along a line segment to fixed points is convex, this critical point gives the minimum. Therefore
PB + PE = 2/sqrt(3) + 1/sqrt(3) = 3/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3).

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus $ABCD$ is 2, and $\angle ADC=120^\circ$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of side $AB$, and point $P$ is a moving point on the diagonal $AC$. What is the minimum value of $PB+PE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect BD, DE, and DE intersects AC at point P$^{\prime}$. Connect BP$^{\prime}$,

$\because$ rhombus ABCD,

$\therefore$ point B and point D are symmetrical about AC,

$\therefore$ DP$^{\prime}$=BP$^{\prime}$,

$\therefore$ P$^{\prime}$B + P$^{\prime}$E = DP$^{\prime}$ + P$^{\prime}$E = DE,

$\because$ the line segment between two points is the shortest,

$\therefore$ the minimum value of P$^{\prime}$B + P$^{\prime}$E is equal to the length of DE;

$\because$ rhombus ABCD,

$\therefore$ DC$\parallel$AB, AD=AB,

$\therefore$ $\angle$ADC + $\angle$DAB = 180$^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle$DAB = 60$^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\triangle$ADB is an equilateral triangle,

$\because$ point E is the midpoint of AB,

$\therefore$ DE $\perp$ AB, BE=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=1, BD=AB=2,

In $\triangle$BDE, $BE=\sqrt{BD^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}}=\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore$ the minimum value of PB+PE is $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a rhombus ABCD, with vertices roughly A on the left, D on top, C on the right, and B on the bottom, forming the rhombus in the order A-D-C-B; diagonal AC has been drawn, point P is located on AC; point E is located on side AB, and line segments such as PE and PB are also drawn in the figure. The problem states that the side length of the rhombus is 2, ∠ADC=120°, E is the midpoint of AB, and P moves on diagonal AC. Reasoning: According to the reflection shortest-path method, in the rhombus, diagonal AC is the axis of symmetry of B and D, so for any P∈AC, PB=PD. Therefore PB+PE=PD+PE. To make the broken-line path from D to P and then to E shortest, with P restricted to AC, the shortest case is that D, P, and E are collinear, that is, P is taken as the intersection point of DE and AC, and at this time the minimum value is equal to DE. Now calculate DE: Because AB∥DC, ∠DAB+∠ADC=180°. Given ∠ADC=120°, therefore ∠DAB=60°. Also AD=AB=2, so △ADB is an equilateral triangle, BD=2. E is the midpoint of AB, so BE=1, and DE is the altitude of equilateral triangle ADB. Thus DE=√(BD²−BE²)=√(2²−1²)=√3. Therefore the minimum value of PB+PE is √3.
